title: Social Loafing
equation: Effort per Person = Group Output ÷ (People × Solo Output)
hook: Put ten people on a task and somehow each one does less than when it was three.
statement: The bigger the group, the less effort each person actually puts in.
explainer: In a crowd, responsibility gets fuzzy and each person's work feels less visible. So everyone coasts a little. More hands, less effort each.
sop: Pick one group task and note its Group Output.
Estimate one capable person's Solo Output on the same work.
Divide Group Output by People × Solo Output.
If it's well below 1, split the work into owned pieces.
Give each piece one name and keep the team small.
equation_example: Group Output 800 ÷ (10 People × 100 Solo Output) = 800 ÷ 1,000 = 0.8. Each person is giving 80% of what they'd do alone. Below 1 means effort is getting lost in the crowd. At 1, everyone's pulling full weight.
question: Pick one shared task and put a single person's name on it.
closing_statement: People do their best work when their name's on it.
caption:
Principle Nº 342: Social Loafing

Put ten people on a task and somehow each one does less than when it was three.

The bigger the group, the less effort each person actually puts in.
